# `format-changed`

Format changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `error` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `format-changed` (both directions), `format-changed-in-request`, `format-changed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

The `format` changed, e.g. `date-time` → `date`. Some changes count as widening (e.g. `int32` → `int64` in requests).

## Why this default

Clients send or parse values in the old format.

## Example

From test case [`format-changed`](../../test/cases/format-changed/): date-time → date in a response.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-           format: date-time
+           format: date
```

Findings:

- `format-changed-in-response` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

2 test cases expect this rule. Each folder has the base and revision documents and the expected findings; they run with `npm test`.

| Test case | Expects | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| [`format-changed`](../../test/cases/format-changed/) | `format-changed-in-response` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet | date-time → date in a response. |
| [`format-changed-widening`](../../test/cases/format-changed-widening/) | `format-changed-in-request` · info · #/components/schemas/Pet | int32 → int64 in a request is widening, so info. |

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

Options for this rule:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `widening` | `{ int32: int64, float: double }` | Format changes treated as widening. |
| `equivalent` | `[]` | Formats that count as the same, e.g. `[[date-time, datetime]]`. |

```yaml
rules:
  format-changed: error
```

## How to fix

Add a new property with the new format.
